title: Registration data can identify the parent directly
description: The registration flow carries strong identifiers and quasi-identifiers including email, full name, government ID, and a six-digit code. If observed or improperly accessed, these data can directly identify the parent and reveal account creation activity.
assumptions: The flow is transmitted, logged, or otherwise handled in a way that could be accessed by unauthorized parties or internal components beyond strict need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for identifiability from a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Registration submissions may be linkable across sessions and systems
description: Stable attributes in the registration payload, especially email and government ID, allow records from this flow to be linked to other datasets, prior visits, or future authentication events, enabling profile building about the parent.
assumptions: The same identifiers are reused across systems or retained over time by the service or related components.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability based on stable identifiers in the flow.

title: Authentication service can detect sensitive parent enrollment behavior
description: By receiving the full registration payload, the authentication service can observe that a specific individual is enrolling, when they enroll, and which identifiers they provide. This creates a detectability risk around the parent's use of the service.
assumptions: Service-side observation, logs, monitoring, or metadata retention make enrollment events visible beyond what is strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for detectability of service use/event occurrence.

title: Sensitive registration attributes may be disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The flow contains highly sensitive personal data, particularly the password and government ID. If the data are intercepted in transit, exposed in logs, or accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, private information about the parent is disclosed.
assumptions: Transport protection, secret handling, and logging controls may be insufficient or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for disclosure of data in transit/processing.

title: Parent may be unable to prove or dispute what registration data were submitted
description: If the service does not provide verifiable submission records or tamper-evident audit trails, the parent may later be unable to demonstrate whether a specific registration request or government ID was submitted, while the service may also struggle to resolve disputes accurately.
assumptions: Registration events are not bound to verifiable receipts, user-visible confirmations, or integrity-protected audit logs.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation can be less central in some privacy analyses of a simple registration flow; node id is a best-effort approximation.

title: Use of government ID and six-digit code may be insufficiently transparent or mislead the parent
description: The flow requests a government ID and a six-digit code during registration. If the interface or backend does not clearly explain why these attributes are needed, how they will be used, or whether they are mandatory, the parent may not understand the privacy implications of providing them.
assumptions: Collection notices, inline explanations, or consent/choice mechanisms are unclear, incomplete, or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for unawareness due to unclear data collection and purpose explanation.

title: Collection of registration data may exceed necessity or legal basis
description: Collecting government ID, name, email, password, and a six-digit code at initial registration may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, storage limitation, or consent/legal-basis requirements if all fields are not strictly necessary for account creation and verification.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements constrain which attributes may be collected and when, and the service may not have documented necessity for each field.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for policy/compliance risk; exact subnode depends on the relevant obligation (e.g., minimization, purpose limitation, lawful basis).

title: Stored parent account data may reveal identity
description: Storing a parent account record in the users collection can directly reveal the identity of the parent through identifiers such as name, email address, phone number, username, or account id if the datastore is accessed by unauthorized parties or used beyond the expected purpose.
assumptions: The parent account contains direct identifiers or account attributes that can identify a natural person.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary depending on whether the schema stores direct identifiers versus only pseudonymous account references.

title: Parent account records may be linkable across contexts
description: A stored parent account in a central users collection can be linked with other records, sessions, child accounts, device data, or service interactions, enabling correlation of the parent's activities across contexts.
assumptions: The same account identifier or stable attributes are reused across multiple collections, services, or events.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate; linkability may map to a different subtree depending on whether the linkage is via identifiers, metadata, or cross-dataset correlation.

title: Presence of a parent account in the users collection may be detectable
description: An attacker or unauthorized internal user may be able to determine whether a particular parent has an account by querying, enumerating, or inferring from datastore contents or application behavior tied to the stored record.
assumptions: Some interface, query path, side channel, or error behavior allows inference about whether a parent account record exists.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping; detectability could also be realized indirectly through application responses rather than direct datastore access.

title: Stored parent account attributes may enable disclosure of personal details
description: The users collection may hold sensitive personal details about the parent, such as contact information, relationship to a child, authentication metadata, or profile data, which could be disclosed through unauthorized access, excessive internal access, backup exposure, or misconfiguration.
assumptions: The parent account record contains personal or potentially sensitive attributes beyond a minimal opaque identifier.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; disclosure severity depends on the actual fields stored in the parent account document.

title: Repurposing stored parent account data may enable unawareness
description: If parent account data is stored without clear, accessible notice about what fields are retained, how long they are kept, and what secondary uses may occur, the parent may be unaware of the processing performed on their stored account data.
assumptions: Transparency mechanisms may be incomplete or insufficiently specific for datastore retention and downstream uses.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on organizational transparency practices not visible from the DFD alone; node id is therefore a best estimate.

title: Storing parent account data may exceed necessity or legal basis
description: The flow may store more parent account information than is necessary for authentication or account management, or retain it without an appropriate legal basis, purpose limitation, or retention control, leading to non-compliance with privacy obligations.
assumptions: The stored record may include unnecessary attributes, excessive retention, or insufficient policy controls for lawful processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; non-compliance often depends on jurisdiction, lawful basis, minimization, and retention details not provided in the DFD.

title: Overexposure of identity attributes in authentication response
description: The authentication service sends a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If the returned user data includes more attributes than are necessary for the parent's immediate purpose, sensitive or identifying information about the authenticated subject may be disclosed to the recipient or to anyone who can access the recipient's device/session.
assumptions: Assumes the user data may contain profile or account attributes beyond the minimum needed to complete login.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for attribute disclosure in a response flow; exact LINDDUN Pro node labeling may vary.

title: Linkability via stable JWT identifiers or repeated claims
description: If the JWT contains stable identifiers, persistent subject claims, or other unique values, the parent user or other parties with access to tokens can correlate multiple sessions or actions belonging to the same individual across time or contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT includes persistent identifiers such as subject IDs, account IDs, or consistent claim combinations.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability caused by persistent identifiers in protocol/application messages.

title: Detectability of account existence or authentication state
description: Differences in the presence, structure, or content of the JWT and accompanying user data can reveal whether a specific person has an account, has successfully authenticated, or has a particular role/status. An observer or recipient may thus detect personal facts even without full access to all backend data.
assumptions: Assumes the flow behavior or payload differs depending on whether authentication succeeds and what type of user is involved.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability through observable message content; exact node mapping may differ.

title: Identifiability from JWT claims and returned user data
description: The JWT and returned user data may directly identify the individual through names, email addresses, account identifiers, or indirectly identifying combinations of attributes, allowing the parent user or others with access to the message to identify the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes the token or user data includes direct or indirect identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct/indirect identifiability in transmitted identity data.

title: Excessive personal data shared without data minimization or purpose limitation
description: Sending both a JWT and user data to the parent may exceed what is necessary for authentication, conflicting with privacy expectations and compliance obligations if the recipient only needs a limited subset of information.
assumptions: Assumes the parent only needs proof of authentication or a minimal profile rather than the full returned user dataset.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to unnecessary disclosure/minimization; exact node id may vary.

title: Insufficient evidence of recipient-side receipt or acceptance of privacy notice/terms
description: If the authentication flow returns JWT and user data without recording that the parent user received or acknowledged any relevant privacy notice, consent context, or data-sharing terms, disputes may arise about what information was provided and under what conditions.
assumptions: Assumes notice/consent or privacy terms are relevant to this authentication-related data transfer and are not separately logged.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related privacy threats are often context-dependent here; inclusion is lower confidence and node id is approximate.

title: Repeated login submissions can link sessions to the same child account or household
description: The child login flow transmits a stable identifier (parent email) together with a password. Even if the child is not named explicitly, repeated use of the same email across sessions can allow the authentication service or observers with access to logs to link multiple login attempts and associated events to the same child account or household.
assumptions: Assumes the parent email is a persistent account identifier and that login attempts or metadata are logged or otherwise observable within the system.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability of repeated messages using a persistent identifier; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Parent email in login flow can identify the child or household
description: The login request contains the parent email, which is directly identifying for the parent and can indirectly identify the child through the family relationship or account records. Anyone with access to the flow, captured requests, or logs may identify the household behind the child's use of the service.
assumptions: Assumes the parent email is unique and associated with the child's account in backend records.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability via direct identifiers in message contents.

title: Authentication service can detect child's use and login patterns
description: By receiving login attempts with parent email and password, the authentication service can detect when the child is active, how often login attempts occur, approximate time of use, and potentially failed-login behavior. This reveals behavioral patterns about the child account or household.
assumptions: Assumes the service records authentication events and timestamps as part of normal operation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/observability of user activity by the receiving process.

title: Login credentials and metadata may be disclosed through transmission or logging
description: The flow carries sensitive credentials (password) and personal data (parent email). If transport protection, endpoint protection, or log handling are inadequate, these data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through interception, debugging traces, application logs, or monitoring systems.
assumptions: Assumes there is some risk of inadequate TLS, credential logging, or overbroad operational access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of sensitive data in transit or at the receiving process; exact subtree may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Authentication service may be unaware of child's expectations around use of parent credentials
description: A child logging in with a parent email may not fully understand what data are collected during authentication, how login attempts are monitored, or how use of a parent's identifier affects privacy. This creates a risk that the data subject is insufficiently aware of processing tied to the login flow.
assumptions: Assumes the product is child-facing and privacy information is not presented in a child-comprehensible manner at login.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of data subject awareness/transparency; node naming may differ.

title: Child login flow may process parent email and child-related data without valid child-appropriate consent or legal basis
description: Because the login uses a parent's email for a child user, the authentication flow may involve processing children's personal data and parent identifiers under legal regimes requiring parental authorization, age-appropriate notices, purpose limitation, and minimization. If these are not properly implemented, the flow may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes the service is subject to child privacy requirements or similar data protection obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for policy/consent/legal-basis non-compliance in an authentication context; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: JWT enables linkability of child sessions across relying components
description: If the JWT contains a stable child identifier or otherwise unique claims, any recipient or observing component that sees the token can correlate multiple sessions and actions to the same child profile over time, linking behavior across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is presented to multiple backend/frontend components or can be observed in logs, browser storage, or network traces.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability of a persistent identifier in a token; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: JWT and profiles can identify the child user
description: The flow explicitly returns a JWT marked with userType child together with child profiles. If the token or profiles include direct or indirect identifiers such as child ID, username, avatar, school/class, or other distinctive attributes, the child can be identified by the recipient or any party gaining access to the data.
assumptions: Assumes child profiles contain personal attributes beyond a purely anonymous role flag.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability from data content.

title: Child profiles disclose personal attributes beyond authentication need
description: Returning child profiles together with the authentication token may expose more personal data than necessary for login, such as profile metadata, preferences, or account details. This increases privacy risk if the child device, app, or another party accesses the response.
assumptions: Assumes the full or rich child profile is sent immediately after authentication rather than a minimal authorization context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; exact subnode may differ depending on whether the main issue is excessive attributes or exposure to an unauthorized party.

title: Local exposure of JWT and profiles on the child device
description: Once delivered to the Child User endpoint, the JWT and profile data may be exposed through insecure client storage, shared device usage, screenshots, browser caches, or malware on the child device, disclosing sensitive account and profile information.
assumptions: Assumes the child accesses the service on a client device where tokens or profile data may be stored or displayed.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-effort client-side disclosure/storage-related mapping.

title: Use of authentication data for secondary profiling may be unexpected
description: A child user may reasonably expect the JWT to support login only, but the token claims and returned child profiles could also be used for analytics, personalization, behavioral tracking, or cross-service profiling in ways that are not apparent at the time of authentication.
assumptions: Assumes downstream systems may process token claims or profile attributes for purposes beyond strictly necessary authentication/session management.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unexpected secondary use; exact subnode may vary.

title: Authentication response may violate data minimization or child-data protection requirements
description: Sending a JWT plus child profiles in one flow may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose of authentication, potentially conflicting with privacy requirements such as data minimization, purpose limitation, or heightened protections applicable to children's data.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy requirements require only minimal authentication/session data to be returned at login.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact node depends on the governing privacy/control requirements.

title: Collection of identifying child attributes enables direct identification
description: The flow sends a child's name, date of birth, gender, and government ID to Child Profile Management. In combination, these attributes directly identify the child and link the profile to a real-world identity, increasing privacy risk if the process does not strictly need all fields or does not compartmentalize them.
assumptions: Assumes the process stores or otherwise uses the full set of submitted attributes rather than immediately minimizing or tokenizing them.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected from general identifiability concepts; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary.

title: Government ID and demographics enable linkage across systems
description: Government ID together with name, DOB, and gender can be correlated with records in other internal or external systems, allowing the child profile to be linked across contexts and revealing a broader picture of the child's activities or status.
assumptions: Assumes government ID or the attribute combination is stable and reusable across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort mapping to linkability; exact branch may differ.

title: Child profile creation discloses sensitive child personal data to the receiving process
description: This flow discloses special-risk personal data about a child, including government identifier and core demographic details, to the Child Profile Management process. If transmission protections, access controls, or purpose limitations are weak, the receiving side may expose this data to unauthorized parties or broader internal audiences.
assumptions: Assumes this threat concerns disclosure during or immediately after receipt by the process, not downstream storage flows.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node chosen; exact LINDDUN Pro node may be more specific for data in transit or recipient-side exposure.

title: Profile creation may exceed data minimization for the stated purpose
description: Collecting name, DOB, gender, and especially government ID at profile creation may be excessive if all fields are not strictly necessary to create and manage a child profile. This creates a detectability/distinguishability risk by making the child more easily singled out and increasing exposure surface.
assumptions: Assumes at least some fields, particularly government ID, may be optional or unnecessary for initial account/profile setup.
uncertainty_note: Low confidence in exact node id because overcollection/data minimization concerns can map differently in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Parent may be unable to prove or contest submitted child identity details
description: If the system lacks strong submission records, timestamps, or confirmation mechanisms, the parent may later be unable to prove what child details were originally submitted, or the process may be unable to demonstrate the provenance of the provided data. This can create disputes around profile creation or correction.
assumptions: Assumes profile creation has legal or operational significance and that audit evidence may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort fit for non-repudiation concerns in user submissions.

title: Collection of child data may occur without valid consent or proper notice
description: The flow involves creating a child's profile using sensitive identifying information. If the parent is not given clear notice about purposes, retention, sharing, and rights, or if parental authority/consent is not properly verified where required, the collection may be non-compliant with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to privacy requirements for children's data and parental consent/notice obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node chosen; exact LINDDUN Pro node may distinguish consent, transparency, or children's data obligations.

title: Unauthorized access to stored child profiles
description: Child profiles stored in the MongoDB collection may be disclosed to unauthorized internal users, compromised services, or attackers if access controls, query authorization, or database security are insufficient. Because the data concerns children, disclosure may expose sensitive identity, demographic, or behavioral information.
assumptions: The childprofiles collection contains personal data about children and is accessible by one or more application components or administrators.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for stored-data disclosure; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Profiles linkable across records or services through persistent identifiers
description: If child profiles are stored with stable identifiers and reused across contexts, records in the collection may be linked with other datasets or activities, enabling broader profiling of a child over time.
assumptions: The profile includes persistent child identifiers or quasi-identifiers that can be correlated across records or systems.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via identifiers in stored data.

title: Child identity inferable from profile attributes
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized, combinations of profile fields such as age, location, preferences, family context, or usage metadata may allow inference of a specific child's identity.
assumptions: Profiles may contain direct identifiers or sufficiently unique combinations of attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from stored attributes; exact tree mapping may differ.

title: Excessive detail in stored child profiles
description: The store/update flow may write more personal data than necessary for the profile-management purpose, such as rich preferences, historical attributes, or optional fields, increasing privacy impact and attack surface.
assumptions: The application permits collecting or persisting optional or nonessential child profile fields.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data minimization / excessive data collection or storage.

title: Secondary use of child profile data beyond the expected purpose
description: Stored child profile data may later be used for analytics, personalization, recommendations, or sharing with other components in ways not apparent to the child or guardian at the time of profile update.
assumptions: The system may support downstream reuse of profile data beyond direct profile management.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for purpose limitation / unexpected processing.

title: Insufficient proof of profile changes and consent context
description: If the process does not reliably record who initiated a child-profile creation or update, when it occurred, and under what authority or parental consent context, parties may later dispute whether a change was authorized or properly made.
assumptions: Profile updates may require guardian authorization, auditability, or proof of consent/approval.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation of actions on personal data; exact subtree may vary.

title: Storage of child profiles without adequate consent, parental authorization, or retention controls
description: Persisting or updating child profiles may violate privacy obligations if the system lacks valid consent/parental authorization, clear legal basis, age-appropriate handling, or enforces retention longer than necessary.
assumptions: The application is subject to child-data compliance obligations and profile records may be retained over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ depending on whether the focus is consent, legal basis, or retention.

title: Search, like, and comment activity can be linked to the same child account or device
description: The video search, request, like, and comment events sent to the Video Management Service can be correlated over time and linked to the same child user profile, account, cookie, IP address, or device identifier. This enables building a detailed viewing and engagement history for the child.
assumptions: The service stores or can observe persistent identifiers or stable metadata across multiple requests.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability at a generic level; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Viewing interests and engagement may reveal the child's identity or profile
description: Search terms, requested videos, likes, and comments may directly identify the child or indirectly reveal identity, age range, school, location, interests, routines, or other attributes when combined with account data or network metadata.
assumptions: Queries or comments may contain personal data, and the service can associate requests with subscriber/account/network metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability; exact node numbering may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Video search and interaction data may disclose sensitive interests or personal information
description: The content of search requests, video requests, likes, and especially free-text comments can disclose sensitive information about the child, such as health concerns, emotional state, religion, sexuality, political views, or other private interests. Disclosure may occur to internal staff, analytics systems, advertisers, or unauthorized parties if broadly accessed or shared.
assumptions: The service logs request contents and/or shares them internally or externally for operations, analytics, moderation, or personalization.
uncertainty_note: Generic disclosure node chosen as best fit; exact subtree for content disclosure may differ.

title: The child may be unaware of collection and downstream use of search and engagement data
description: A child user may not understand that searches, viewed videos, likes, and comments are recorded, profiled, retained, and potentially shared for recommendation, moderation, analytics, or advertising-related purposes, reducing predictability of processing.
assumptions: Notices are limited, complex, or not presented in a child-comprehensible way.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/non-transparency style node; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Search and engagement data may be processed beyond the child's expectations or meaningful consent
description: The service may use the child's search history, likes, comments, and viewing requests for profiling, personalization, experimentation, or sharing with third parties without valid parental authorization or age-appropriate, understandable consent/assent mechanisms.
assumptions: The child is below the age for independent valid consent and parental authorization or equivalent legal basis may be required.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unawareness/consent deficiency; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Collection and use of child interaction data may violate child-privacy and data minimization requirements
description: Collecting detailed search logs, video requests, likes, and comments from a child may exceed what is necessary for service delivery, or may be retained/shared in ways inconsistent with child-privacy obligations, purpose limitation, retention limits, or parental-rights requirements.
assumptions: Applicable laws or platform commitments impose heightened requirements for children's data, minimization, retention, transparency, and parental controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: The child may be unable to later deny a like or comment attributed to them
description: If the service keeps persistent logs binding likes or comments to the child account or device, those records may later be used as evidence that the child performed a specific action, even if the action was accidental, coerced, or performed by someone else using the device/account.
assumptions: The service keeps attributable logs with timestamps and identifiers, and account/device sharing is possible.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation through attributable action logs; exact subtree may differ.

title: Linkability of video records across uploads and access events
description: Persistent identifiers in stored video metadata (e.g., account ID, device ID, uploader ID, channel ID, IP-derived attributes, or stable file hashes) can allow records in the videos collection to be linked across multiple uploads, edits, views, and other systems, enabling profiling of a person's activity over time.
assumptions: The videos collection stores stable user, device, or content identifiers together with metadata and access-related attributes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Identifiability from stored video metadata
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB may directly identify individuals through names, usernames, account identifiers, email addresses, profile references, facial thumbnails, or indirectly through unique combinations of timestamp, title, location, and device metadata.
assumptions: Stored metadata includes direct or quasi-identifiers associated with uploaders, subjects, or viewers.
uncertainty_note: Node id chosen as a generic identifiability-from-data-store fit; exact node label may differ.

title: Disclosure of personal data via overbroad storage of metadata
description: The flow stores video-related metadata in the videos collection; if more personal data than necessary is retained, or if sensitive metadata such as location, device details, private visibility settings, moderation flags, or access history is included, unauthorized parties or internal actors may learn personal information from the stored records.
assumptions: The collection may hold rich metadata beyond what is strictly needed for core video management.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure from stored data; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may differ.

title: Lack of data minimization and retention controls for video metadata
description: Storing video metadata and references to files without clear retention limits or minimization can lead to prolonged retention of personal data, including historical versions, deleted-video remnants, moderation outcomes, and obsolete identifiers, increasing privacy risk over time.
assumptions: Records may persist after user deletion, replacement, or account closure unless explicit lifecycle controls exist.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed approximation for excessive retention / minimization issues.

title: Users may be unaware that extensive metadata is stored with videos
description: When the Video Management Service writes data to the videos collection, users may not understand that uploads can result in storage of auxiliary metadata such as timestamps, technical file properties, inferred categories, moderation annotations, location, or linkage to account activity, preventing informed expectations about processing.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-product explanations may be incomplete regarding metadata stored alongside uploaded videos.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for insufficient transparency/awareness; exact node id may differ by threat-tree version.

title: Storage of video metadata without a valid legal basis or beyond stated purpose
description: If the service stores metadata or file-related attributes in MongoDB beyond what is necessary for providing video functionality, or reuses it for analytics, profiling, or moderation purposes not covered by the original purpose or consent, the processing may be non-compliant with data protection obligations.
assumptions: Some stored fields may support secondary uses or exceed the purpose communicated to users.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unlawful or purpose-incompatible processing; exact node id may vary.

title: Insufficient evidence of user actions on metadata changes
description: If updates to video metadata in the collection are not attributable with privacy-preserving audit records, users or operators may later be unable to demonstrate whether a title, visibility setting, deletion request, or ownership attribute was changed, hindering resolution of disputes about personal-data handling.
assumptions: The system may lack trustworthy and proportionate audit trails for metadata creation, modification, and deletion events.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability is somewhat context-dependent for this storage flow; node id is approximate.

title: Stored child search/watch history can identify a specific child profile
description: Writing detailed search and watch history to the childprofiles collection may allow the stored records to directly or indirectly identify a child profile, especially when combined with profile identifiers, timestamps, device/account context, or unique viewing patterns.
assumptions: The history is stored together with a child profile key or other account-linked metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; using a generic identifiability node because exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Accumulated history in the childprofiles store enables linking of a child's activities over time
description: Central storage of search and watch history in one collection enables linking multiple events to the same child profile across sessions and over long periods, revealing behavior patterns, interests, routines, or household context.
assumptions: Records in DS2 are keyed or otherwise consistently associated with the same child profile over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro linkability subtree id may differ.

title: Search and watch history reveals sensitive preferences and behaviors
description: The stored history may disclose personal interests, habits, emotional state, developmental stage, religious/cultural interests, health-related concerns, or other sensitive inferences about a child. Unauthorized access or secondary use would expose private information.
assumptions: History includes sufficiently granular titles, queries, categories, timestamps, or recommendations to support sensitive inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; using a generic detectability/disclosure-related node because exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Retention or reuse of child history may exceed user or regulatory expectations
description: Persisting child search and watch history in the childprofiles collection may be non-compliant if collection, retention period, purpose limitation, parental transparency, or lawful basis are not appropriately defined for children's data.
assumptions: The system is subject to children's privacy obligations or has stated privacy commitments limiting such storage/use.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact non-compliance subtree id may vary depending on the LINDDUN Pro catalog used.

title: Users may be unaware that child search and watch history is being persisted
description: If the Child Profile Management process stores history without clear notice or understandable controls, parents or guardians may not be adequately aware of what data is stored, for how long, and for what purposes, undermining transparency and intervenability.
assumptions: Notice/consent and profile-level privacy controls may be limited or not clearly presented at the time history is generated.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; using a generic unawareness node because exact subtree numbering may differ.

title: Video upload can reveal the child's and parent's identity
description: The uploaded video may contain direct identifiers (faces, voices, names in speech or metadata) and contextual clues, allowing the service to identify the child and parent.
assumptions: The service stores or inspects uploaded video and associated metadata for approval/rejection.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for identifiability from content/metadata; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Uploaded video and decision records can be linked to the parent's account across submissions
description: Because the upload is sent by a logged-in parent user to the video management service, the service can link this video, its metadata, and the approval/rejection outcome to the same account over time, enabling profiling of submission history.
assumptions: Parent uploads are authenticated or otherwise associated with a stable account or device identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability across multiple items/transactions; numbering may be approximate.

title: Approval/rejection decision may disclose sensitive inferences about the video content
description: The service's approval or rejection response can reveal information about the child, parent, or circumstances shown in the video, such as policy-violating behavior, sensitive attributes, or home environment details inferred during moderation.
assumptions: The outcome or accompanying reason is visible to parties beyond the minimal need-to-know, or retained in logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of information through system outputs/decisions; exact node id may differ.

title: Parent may be unaware of moderation, retention, or secondary use of uploaded videos
description: If the upload flow does not clearly explain how videos are reviewed, how long they are retained, who can access them, and whether they are reused for training or quality control, the parent may be insufficiently informed about processing.
assumptions: Transparency notices in the upload interface may be incomplete or hard to understand.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact numbering may vary.

title: Video processing for approval/rejection may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: If uploaded videos are later used for analytics, model training, employee review beyond moderation, or retained longer than necessary, the processing may violate consent, purpose limitation, or data minimization expectations.
assumptions: The service may have secondary processing activities not fully aligned with the original upload purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with consent/purpose limitation obligations; exact node id may differ.

title: Lack of proof about submission and moderation actions can create repudiation issues
description: If the system does not keep trustworthy records of who uploaded the video, when it was uploaded, and who or what approved/rejected it, either party may later dispute the submission or moderation outcome.
assumptions: Audit trails, timestamps, or integrity protections may be weak or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation of action/events; exact numbering may vary.

title: Excessive or unnecessary video data may be collected during upload
description: Full video files can capture far more personal data than needed for the approval decision, including background people, location clues, voices, and device metadata, increasing the risk of detectability and overexposure.
assumptions: The service accepts raw video uploads without minimization, trimming, or metadata stripping.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability/data presence due to unnecessary data collection; exact node id may be approximate.

title: Exposure of child's viewing choice to network observers
description: If the video stream or related metadata is not adequately protected in transit, intermediaries or eavesdroppers could learn which approved video is being delivered to the child, revealing viewing preferences or interests.
assumptions: Assumes the stream or its metadata may be observable on the network path, especially if transport encryption or traffic-analysis protections are weak.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on generic disclosure during transmission; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may differ.

title: Linkability of multiple viewing sessions for the same child
description: Persistent identifiers, stable session tokens, or distinctive stream-request patterns may allow the child's separate viewing sessions to be linked together, enabling profiling over time.
assumptions: Assumes the service, delivery infrastructure, or observers can see stable identifiers or recurring metadata across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers across interactions.

title: Identifiability of the child through stream metadata or account context
description: Metadata accompanying the video stream, such as account identifiers, device identifiers, or precise timing information, may make the child user identifiable to the service, CDN, or third parties handling delivery.
assumptions: Assumes the child is associated with an account, household profile, or device-level identifiers during streaming.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct or indirect identifiability from transmitted identifiers; exact subtree may vary.

title: Inference of sensitive attributes from streamed content
description: The specific approved video being streamed may disclose sensitive information about the child, such as age band, developmental status, language, interests, or special-category inferences, to parties able to observe the flow.
assumptions: Assumes the chosen video title/category correlates with personal characteristics and can be inferred from traffic, URLs, headers, or CDN logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for sensitive content inference from the data flow.

title: Child may be unaware of what streaming data and metadata are exposed
description: The child user may not understand that receiving a video stream also exposes metadata such as viewing time, device information, and content selection to the service or delivery partners, reducing transparency.
assumptions: Assumes limited transparency toward the child and that the child is not capable of fully understanding the processing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for insufficient awareness/transparency affecting this flow.

title: Streaming to a child without valid, context-appropriate consent or authorization basis
description: Delivering the video stream may involve processing children's personal data and viewing behavior without a valid legal basis, parental authorization, or age-appropriate consent mechanism where required.
assumptions: Assumes this flow is part of regulated child-directed processing and consent/authorization obligations apply.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact node mapping depends on the LINDDUN Pro compliance subtree used.

title: Linkability of child browsing records across sessions and services
description: Browsing data stored in the childprofiles collection may contain persistent identifiers or stable behavioral patterns that allow the AI Recommendation Engine to link a child's activity across sessions, devices, or contexts, enabling construction of a unified profile.
assumptions: Assumes records include account IDs, device IDs, cookies, timestamps, or sufficiently distinctive browsing-history features.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability from persistent/behavioral identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Identification of a child from browsing data
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized, the AI engine may be able to identify an individual child by combining browsing history, timestamps, preferences, and other quasi-identifiers received from the data store.
assumptions: Assumes the flow includes rich event history or metadata and the AI engine has access to auxiliary data or account context.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; threat is identification via quasi-identifiers/inference from the received dataset.

title: Inference of sensitive child attributes from browsing behavior
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may derive sensitive information about a child, such as health concerns, emotional state, religion, vulnerabilities, or special educational needs, from the browsing data sent for recommendation purposes.
assumptions: Assumes the model performs profiling or feature extraction beyond simple content matching.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/disclosure-related inference node; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may differ.

title: Use of child browsing data beyond parental or expected purpose
description: Browsing data collected for operating the child profile may be repurposed by the AI Recommendation Engine for personalization, model improvement, analytics, or experimentation without being adequately separated from the original purpose or user expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the AI pipeline may retain inputs for secondary uses such as training, tuning, or metrics.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is a classic purpose non-compliance / secondary-use threat.

title: Children or guardians may be unaware of AI profiling from browsing data
description: If the transfer from the childprofiles collection to the AI Recommendation Engine is only planned or insufficiently explained, children and guardians may not understand that browsing activity is being analyzed to generate recommendations or profiles.
assumptions: Assumes notices, dashboards, or consent flows do not clearly describe this data use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact subtree numbering may vary.

title: Processing child browsing data without valid consent or other lawful basis
description: Sending child browsing data to the AI Recommendation Engine may violate children's privacy requirements if explicit parental consent, age-appropriate transparency, data minimization, or other legal obligations for profiling minors are not met.
assumptions: Assumes the jurisdiction requires parental consent or strict safeguards for profiling children.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact numbering may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Advertisers can link browsing data to identifiable users across contexts
description: Browsing data disclosed by the AI Recommendation Engine to third-party advertisers may contain direct or indirect identifiers, stable pseudonyms, device/browser fingerprints, or granular behavioral patterns that let advertisers link records to the same individual over time and across services.
assumptions: Assumes the planned data sharing includes persistent identifiers or sufficiently granular event/context data to support record linkage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability of shared records; exact subtree naming may vary by LINDDUN Pro edition.

title: Browsing data may enable identification of individuals by advertisers
description: Even if the transmitted browsing data is presented as pseudonymous, advertisers may combine it with their existing customer, tracking, or broker datasets to identify the person behind the browsing behavior.
assumptions: Assumes third-party advertisers possess auxiliary datasets or identifiers that can be matched with the shared browsing data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identification via combination with auxiliary data.

title: Browsing history disclosure to third parties reveals user interests and behavior
description: Sending browsing data to advertisers exposes potentially sensitive information about pages viewed, products considered, interests, habits, time patterns, and inferred characteristics, creating a disclosure of personal information to an external party.
assumptions: Assumes the flow contains detailed browsing events, URLs, categories, timestamps, or inferred interests rather than only coarse aggregated statistics.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node id; exact numbering may differ.

title: Advertisers may infer sensitive attributes from browsing data
description: Third-party advertisers can derive or detect sensitive traits such as health concerns, political interests, religion, sexual orientation, financial stress, or other special-category information from detailed browsing behavior, even if such traits are not explicitly sent.
assumptions: Assumes browsing data is sufficiently detailed to support profiling or sensitive inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/inference of sensitive information from observable data.

title: Users may be unaware that browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers
description: Because this is a planned secondary use of browsing data, data subjects may not expect or understand that their behavior is being transferred from the recommendation engine to external advertisers for advertising purposes.
assumptions: Assumes notice is absent, unclear, buried, or inconsistent with user expectations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient user awareness/transparency; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Sharing browsing data with advertisers may exceed the original purpose or valid legal basis
description: Using recommendation-system browsing data for third-party advertising may be incompatible with the original collection purpose, may lack valid consent or another lawful basis, and may breach data minimization, purpose limitation, or third-party sharing commitments.
assumptions: Assumes the browsing data was originally collected for personalization/recommendation and not clearly for external advertising disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance relating to purpose limitation/legal basis; exact numbering may differ.

title: Insufficient proof of user consent or advertiser receipt terms may enable repudiation
description: If consent records, sharing logs, or contractual acknowledgements are incomplete, the sender may be unable to prove that disclosure to advertisers was authorized, and advertisers may later dispute what data was received or under what restrictions.
assumptions: Assumes weak logging, consent capture, or data-sharing accountability controls around the planned flow.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow than disclosure/linkability; node id is a best-fit.

title: Stored government ID images can reveal highly sensitive personal attributes
description: Government ID images stored in the uploads file system may expose direct identifiers and sensitive personal data such as full name, date of birth, ID number, address, photograph, and nationality to unauthorized parties or internal actors. Because the flow persists full images rather than a minimized attribute set, confidentiality impact is high.
assumptions: The file system stores the raw image files and they may be accessible to system administrators, backup operators, or compromised application components beyond the strict need-to-know boundary.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro disclosure subtree labeling may vary.

title: Government ID images in persistent storage enable strong linkability across sessions and systems
description: A stored government ID image contains stable identifiers and biometric/photo content that can be used to link the same individual across authentication attempts, accounts, databases, or external datasets. Centralized storage in the file system increases the chance that records associated with one context are correlated with others.
assumptions: The stored files are retained with filenames, metadata, account references, or hashes that can be correlated across events or systems.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers in stored content.

title: Stored ID images make users identifiable beyond what is necessary
description: The raw image directly identifies a person through face photograph and official identity details. If the purpose is only age, residency, or account verification, retaining the full image in the file system creates unnecessary identifiability and increases privacy risk.
assumptions: Business purpose could potentially be met by storing extracted verification status or a redacted/minimized record instead of the full image.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact identifiability subtree numbering may differ.

title: Excessive retention of uploaded ID images increases detectability of sensitive participation
description: Persisting government ID images in backend/uploads/ may allow an observer with access to the datastore, backups, or file listings to detect that a specific person underwent identity verification or attempted to use the service. This can reveal account enrollment or service usage patterns even without opening every file.
assumptions: File names, timestamps, directory structure, or associated metadata can be inspected and correlated to individuals or accounts.
uncertainty_note: Detectability is inferred from the existence of stored artifacts and metadata; node id is approximate.

title: Storing full government ID images may exceed necessity, proportionality, or legal basis
description: The authentication service sends full government ID images to persistent storage, which may violate data minimization, storage limitation, or purpose limitation requirements if only a verification decision or a limited subset of attributes is needed. This creates a non-compliance risk under privacy and identity-document handling obligations.
assumptions: Applicable laws, contractual obligations, or internal policy require minimizing or limiting retention of official identity documents.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact node numbering may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Insufficient evidence around image upload/storage may let parties dispute collection or handling
description: If the system does not maintain trustworthy records of user submission, consent/notice, verification purpose, and storage actions for government ID images, the service or user may later be unable to prove whether an image was provided, stored, accessed, or deleted. This creates repudiation-related privacy and accountability issues around highly sensitive documents.
assumptions: Audit trails for this storage flow may be incomplete, mutable, or not bound to user notice/consent records.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability depends on whether auditable evidence is part of the design; node id is approximate.

title: JWT in localStorage can be read by unauthorized scripts or users
description: Storing a JWT in browser localStorage exposes the token to any script running in the page origin, including malicious injected JavaScript or over-privileged third-party code. If the JWT contains personal data in cleartext or can be used to retrieve personal data, confidentiality is lost.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is accessible to client-side scripts and may contain claims about the user or grant access to personal data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure from a data store; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may differ.

title: Persistent JWT enables cross-session linkability
description: A long-lived JWT stored in localStorage can act as a stable pseudonymous identifier. Reuse of the same token value or stable claims across visits allows actions and sessions in the same browser to be linked together.
assumptions: Assumes token lifetime or token contents are sufficiently stable to correlate multiple sessions or visits.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability due to a persistent identifier in client storage; exact subnode may vary.

title: JWT claims may disclose identity to local observers or scripts
description: JWTs often include subject identifiers, email addresses, roles, or other claims. When stored in localStorage, these claims may be exposed to anyone or any code with access to the browser context, revealing the user's identity.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is not encrypted and contains directly identifying or easily attributable claims.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability arising from exposed identity-bearing token claims; exact node id may differ.

title: JWT contents may reveal sensitive personal attributes
description: Claims inside the JWT may reveal personal data beyond identity, such as roles, group memberships, tenant affiliation, or other attributes. Storing the token in localStorage increases the chance that such data becomes visible to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the token payload includes privacy-relevant claims and is readable by client-side code or local users.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of information from token contents; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: LocalStorage persistence may exceed user expectations or consent
description: localStorage persists until explicitly cleared. Storing authentication tokens there may retain personal-data-bearing artifacts longer than necessary, undermining storage limitation and potentially conflicting with user expectations, consent, or policy commitments.
assumptions: Assumes no strict retention controls or user-visible notice govern the token's persistence in the browser.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best fit for non-compliance due to excessive retention/persistence; exact subnode may differ.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child history to the wrong parent account
description: If Child Profile Management sends a child's history to an incorrectly authenticated, misbound, or shared parent account, sensitive information about the child may be exposed to someone who should not have access.
assumptions: Assumes parent authorization is enforced by or before P3 and that child history may contain sensitive behavioral, health, educational, or location-related details.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure via unintended recipient, but exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may differ.

title: Excessive visibility of detailed child history to the parent
description: The flow may reveal more child-history detail than is necessary for the parent's review purpose, enabling profiling or exposure of sensitive events beyond what is proportionate.
assumptions: Assumes the history view could include granular timestamps, third-party notes, or categories not strictly necessary for the stated review purpose.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best match for detectability/inference from overly detailed content; exact subnode may differ.

title: Linkability of child records across contexts through stable identifiers in the history
description: If the returned history includes persistent identifiers, consistent pseudonyms, or cross-context references, the parent can link the child's activities across separate services, periods, or profiles more easily than intended.
assumptions: Assumes the history contains stable identifiers or correlated metadata across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability through shared identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro leaf may vary.

title: Exposure of child history through insecure parent-side handling
description: Once received by the Parent User, child history may be displayed on an unlocked device, cached in a browser, captured in screenshots, or viewed by other household members, causing onward disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes no strong client-side protections or user guidance prevent local exposure after delivery.
uncertainty_note: This is a flow-endpoint disclosure risk grounded at the recipient; node id is approximate.

title: Sharing child history without valid consent, authorization, or legal basis
description: Providing the child's history to the parent may violate applicable privacy requirements if consent, parental rights, age-dependent controls, custody constraints, or other legal bases are absent, outdated, or not verified.
assumptions: Assumes legal authority to access the child's history can vary by jurisdiction, age, guardianship, or record type.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort non-compliance node id for missing lawful basis/authorization; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of what child history was disclosed to which parent
description: If the system does not keep adequate disclosure logs, it may be impossible to prove which parent accessed which child-history items and when, undermining accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: Assumes access/disclosure logging may be incomplete or not tamper-evident.
uncertainty_note: Approximate repudiation-related node id for lack of provable disclosure records.
